name: Jack Reed

issue_poll.name: Combined: UNH Survey Center Ocean State Poll (Nov 1, 2026); Emerson College/WPRI RI poll (May 14-16, 2026); Rhode Island Survey Initiative/YouGov (Jul 29-Aug 13, 2026)
issue_poll.note: UNH Nov 2026 abstract names affordability/inflation and the economy as top issues (no percentages accessible). Emerson May 2026 most-important-issue: economy 31%, housing affordability 21%, health care 12%, infrastructure 10% (others not published). RISI Aug 2026 top priorities for state government ranked the rest: housing 64%, health care 62%, roads/bridges 37%, education 30%, crime 26%, aid to the poor 25%, environment 19%, clean energy 14%. RISI listed no national issues, so Immigration was placed at rank 6 based on UNH's July 2024 RI most-important-problem poll (immigration 6%, tied with education) and its prominence in 2026 national polling. RISI: https://oceanstatestories.org/?p=8052 ; UNH: https://scholars.unh.edu/survey_center_polls/1015

issues.detail: Oppose Trump administration tariffs; seek refunds of tariff costs to consumers.
Calls lowering housing costs a top priority; no specific measure or target stated.
Restore enhanced ACA premium tax credits; address health-industry consolidation and price transparency.
Oppose shifting federal Head Start standards and decisions to the states.
Require ICE agents to be unmasked, show identification, and wear body cameras.
Enact more commonsense gun violence reforms; no specific measure named.
National energy policy limiting carbon pollution; oppose weakening the Clean Water Act.
Oppose further federal halts of Revolution Wind; national policy developing renewable energy.

plan_caveats: Reed ran a low-profile campaign: no campaign issue pages found, no debates held, and few specific forward-looking pledges; most positions come from 2026 interviews and in-office 2026 statements.

Issue ranking combines three polls with different question types (MIP vs state-government priorities); no single 2026 RI poll ranked 10 issues, and UNH Nov 2026 percentages were inaccessible (PDF blocked).
Immigration rank (6) is a judgment call: RISI did not ask national issues; placement uses UNH 2024 RI data and national 2026 polling.
Housing rated Vague from the official Senate issue page only; his housing record (federal funds) is past record and not counted.
Anti-poverty rated None: his SNAP restoration bill (S.3281) plan is a Nov 2025 in-office release, not a 2026 campaign statement; it would otherwise be Concrete.
Infrastructure rated None: he pledged legislation to release denied 2026 blizzard FEMA aid (turnto10, Sep 4 2026), treated as disaster aid rather than roads/bridges.
Environment/climate positions are ecoRI's compilation from his website, not direct campaign answers.
Tariff refund item comes from a March 2026 Senate letter; the campaign framing (opposing tariffs as a reason to run) is from a Feb 2026 interview.
